blocks.p: The core design is sound: server-side access control reloaded on every request, a well-built SSO flow, a gauge scheduler with locks, retries and an archive fallback, transactional migrations, and disciplined per-site time zones. The gaps were in operations (no error logging, shallow health check, no timeouts), deployment (end-of-life Node, unsafe defaults) and performance (full-history reads).

blocks.p: Two hosts on Alibaba Cloud plus a managed database. The browser loads the React app from nginx on the app host, which proxies /api and /auth to the Express API on the API host (private network only). The API reads and writes ApsaraDB PostgreSQL, calls the Hub for sign-in, DataHub for master data, and the TankVision gauges at the plant. Cron on the API host runs the gauge schedule every 5 minutes and the daily purge. Logsheet data arrives from a site PC as JSON files.

blocks.p: **AR-01 Error handler logged nothing; bad JSON returned 500.** Evidence: `index.js:44-49` returned 500 for every error without logging; a malformed body returned the parser's message. Impact: production failures left no trace and client mistakes counted as server errors. Done: `errors.js` and a new handler (logged as JSON; 400/409/413 where the client is at fault; generic 500 body), `asyncErrors.js` so rejected async handlers reach it.

**AR-02 Point-in-time screens read the full site history.** Evidence: `loadSiteTanks` selects every sounding and certificate of a site, twice per site for Stock Overview, refreshed every 60 s per open tab. Impact: load grows linearly with history (about 730 rows per gauged tank per year). Next: query only the needed days, latest certificate per tank, a short per-site cache. Effort M; planned with AR-15.
**AR-03 Node 20 end-of-life; floating image tags.** Done: Node 22 LTS in both Dockerfiles, CI and package engines; nginx pinned to 1.28-alpine. Backend tests pass on Node 22.

**AR-04 Production-unsafe defaults.** Evidence: compose defaults COOKIE_SECURE=false and the legacy bridge on; plain HTTP; no CSP/HSTS. Done: API security headers. Next: production compose must require explicit secure values (fail closed), HTTPS with HSTS at the host nginx, the API bound to the private address, an SPA CSP allowing the Hub frame.

bullets: Server-side RBAC reloaded per request; site and module scoping in middleware; role-grant escalation prevented and tested.
SSO with PKCE, state and nonce, algorithm pinning, maximum token age, single-use replay guard, iframe breakout, verified-e-mail linking.
Gauge scheduler: advisory lock, persisted attempts per round, configurable retries, archive fallback at the round time, backfill script, unit tests.
Migrations: transactional under an advisory lock; CI proves a second run is a no-op.
Per-site time zones; DATE kept as text; round times local to each site.
Secrets encrypted at rest and never returned; .dockerignore excludes env files; the API runs as a non-root user.
Destructive-script guard (--confirm-site); idempotent ingest keyed on business keys.
